speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that. Can you describe what the swelling in your right knee looks like, and do you have any history of joint injuries or surgeries? Also, how old are you and when did you first notice these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Leukemia (Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia) presenting as a bone marrow failure with lytic lesions in the distal femur.

Note: While the knee swelling and family history might initially suggest a genetic bone disorder like osteopetrosis or a specific tumor syndrome, the absence of trauma, the age of the patient, and the nature of the swelling often point towards hematologic malignancies in pediatric cases where the bone is compromised. Immediate blood work and imaging are critical to confirm or rule out leukemia versus a primary bone tumor or metabolic bone disease.

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, ESR, CRP, LFTs, Urinalysis.
REQUEST TEST: X_Ray_Knee_Right.
